svg.title: Estia architecture: one Mac mini at home, reached only through Signal
svg.desc: Diagram of how Estia is wired. In the middle, the mac mini @ home. Inside it: Messages, calls and tools (signal-cli, a headless Signal client, with her Signal account on a spare SIM's number or with no number; an optional call helper; the bridge, her main program; her tools, listed by /tools in Signal); Thinking (Ollama's official build in her own macOS account, or the Ollama app when it is chosen at setup, running Gemma 4, with cloud models refused; and the optional AgentJev, which marks bulk mail before Gemma); Voice, optional (the voice service for speech to text and back, which answers only her own macOS account; Whisper; a speech detector and a turn detector, on calls); Her voices, optional (Pocket TTS, her only voice, made on the Mac's CPU: Heart by default, the others by name; Jane in six more languages; Korean, Polish, Russian and Japanese have no voice, and her answers in them come as text); Helpers (an optional read-only calendar helper, an optional device helper for the home network, a YouTube helper for captions, and the setup window, where your Mac password goes only to macOS's own password box); Memory and files (a SQLite database with chats, memory and mail headers, an optional documents helper that reads your PDFs and needs no network, optional read-only project tools). She runs in her own hidden macOS account; the bridge listens on nothing; there is no web app and no open port; she runs only a root-owned release, which only an update changes. Every Python package is locked to one version by its sha256 hash; known security holes are checked offline with osv-scanner before each release and every week on GitHub, and a known hole stops a release. On the left, your phone and your laptop reach the Mac only through Signal's servers, end-to-end encrypted in both directions, for texts, voice notes, photos, PDFs, locations and calls. The laptop is a linked device: its texts are held, unread, until the phone approves it. The call helper reaches Signal's relay servers itself. On the right, read-only: Microsoft 365 mail and Outlook calendar, Google Calendar, and iCloud, Fastmail, Nextcloud and other CalDAV calendars, which are read and never changed (CalDAV is not tested live); and questions out: Ollama web search, Brave Search as the backup search, web pages (links you send and Brave's top result), YouTube captions, places and routes from OpenStreetMap with no account and no key, and Google Maps, asked first once set up. At the top, downloads into the Mac: the model from the Ollama library and voice models from Hugging Face, once; code and tools from GitHub, Homebrew and crates.io. At the bottom, the home network only: Philips Hue, TP-Link Kasa and Tapo, Bose SoundTouch; and music commands out to Spotify. Limits: only the Signal accounts in the config get an answer, other senders are ignored, never rejected; no cloud AI service, no account with us, no telemetry; no web app and no open port; no shell for the AI; mail is never sent, moved, deleted or marked; calendar events are never created, changed or answered; an answer that reads mail, a project or a document sends nothing to a search engine or a map; mail bodies, YouTube captions, web results and map results are never stored, photos are deleted after the first answer; callers never learn the Mac's IP address: calls use relay-only ICE through Signal's relay servers.
